findings.claim: Without a surrogate, the formatted type T always goes through contractless mode. Any [MessagePackObject]/[Key]/[IgnoreMember] or [DataContract]/[DataMember] attributes on T are ignored. The acceptance criterion says 'If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured' (the maintainer said 'If there are attributes on it, fine, we'll use them'). The change instead serializes every public read-write member under its name as a string key. As a result, members marked [IgnoreMember], or left out of a [DataContract], are still serialized, and [Key(int)] ordinals are replaced by name keys.

receipt_plan.detail: Run tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests/Receipts/GeneratedFormatterHonoursTypeAttributesTests.cs. DataContractOnReferencedTypeIsHonoured and MessagePackAttributesOnReferencedTypeAreHonoured fail on head because the generated MyTypeFormatter body references the excluded member 'Secret'.

findings.claim: The contractless mode here differs from the library's existing contractless behaviour in two ways. First, getter-only public members are silently dropped from serialization. Second, constructor parameters are never matched, so a class whose only constructor takes parameters is rejected with NoDeserializingConstructor. For an immutable type from a dependency-free library, 'contractless behaviour over public members' would therefore either lose data or not generate at all.

receipt_plan.detail: Use the two-compilation harness from GeneratedFormatterReferencedTypeTests with ProjectA.MyType = `public class MyType { public MyType(int id) { Id = id; } public int Id { get; } }`. Assert the ProjectB output compilation has no errors and that a generated tree containing 'class MyTypeFormatter' exists. On head this fails with a NoDeserializingConstructor error and no formatter body.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Contractless means only public, non-static, read-write instance properties and fields, serialized with string keys equal to their names. Deserialization requires an accessible parameterless constructor (classes). Getter-only members are skipped, and types that have only a parameterized constructor are rejected (GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:77 and CreateContractlessMembers using IsPublicReadWrite).

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Contractless means the same member set as the existing DynamicContractlessObjectResolver. Every public readable instance member is serialized, and getter-only members become serialize-only (MemberSerializationInfo.IsWritable = false). The public constructor whose parameters match member names is used for deserialization. Minimal edit: in CreateContractlessMembers, filter by a public-readable predicate and set IsWritable/IsReadable per member. Replace the parameterless-constructor rejection at line 77 with constructor-parameter matching passed as constructorParameters to ObjectSerializationInfo.Create.
